items.label: Penguin Solutions Q4 FY2026 (10-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO Aaron Johnson: Q4 gross margin of 28.8% was up 70 basis

set.signal: Interim CFO Aaron Johnson: Q4 gross margin of 28.8% was up 70 basis points sequentially, supported by improved profitability in Integrated Memory, partially offset by lower Advanced Computing margins; record gross profit of $163 million was up 21% sequentially and 57% year-over-year. Q4 operating expenses were $73 million (up 4% sequentially, 13% year-over-year), and record Q4 operating income of $90 million rose 39% sequentially and 129% year-over-year, with operating margin expanding 2.4 percentage points sequentially and 4.2 percentage points year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was a record $93 million, up 115% year-over-year. Q4 product net sales were $510 million (90% of total), up 86% year-over-year; services net sales were $57 million (10%), down 11% year-over-year, reflecting lower hyperscale services volumes partially offset by growth in multi-year AI factory managed services.

items.label: Penguin Solutions Q4 FY2026 (10-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO Aaron Johnson: full-year FY2026 net sales were $1.73 bil

set.signal: Interim CFO Aaron Johnson: full-year FY2026 net sales were $1.73 billion, up 26% versus fiscal 2025, and diluted EPS rose 51% to $2.87, $0.22 above the high end of the July outlook. Full-year gross profit reached a record $508 million; gross margin was 29.3%, down 1.7 percentage points, primarily due to a greater contribution from AI infrastructure hardware even with stronger Integrated Memory margins. Operating expenses rose 4% to $267 million; operating income reached a record $241 million, up 44%, with operating margin expanding 1.7 percentage points to 13.9%; full-year adjusted EBITDA was $256 million, up 37%.

items.signal_prefix: Supply: in Q4 Penguin established a new supply arrangement w

set.signal: Supply: in Q4 Penguin established a new supply arrangement with a leading memory supplier (unnamed) to support its data center AI infrastructure portfolio and strengthen its supply position, and a relationship with another AI hardware supplier (unnamed) to help expand supply availability. Interim CFO Aaron Johnson: the FY2027 outlook incorporates current assumptions for memory supply and costs, 'which may evolve during the year', including the expected impact of these new memory and AI infrastructure suppliers; certain components continue to have extended lead times that can affect project and shipment timing. Inventory rose to $749 million from $255 million a year ago (inventory days 48), reflecting purchases to support record backlog and expected deployments plus higher memory costs.

items.signal_prefix: Cash flow and operating model: cash used in operating activi

set.signal: Cash flow and operating model: cash used in operating activities was $163 million in Q4 and $152 million for the full year, mainly working capital for the memory and AI infrastructure businesses; net accounts receivable were $796 million and accounts payable $817 million; Penguin ended Q4 with cash and cash equivalents of $647 million. Capital expenditures were $4 million in the quarter and $12 million for the year, and interim CFO Aaron Johnson expects the asset-light model to continue in fiscal 2027. CEO: 95%+ of engineering is in India, memory engineering is in Taiwan and manufacturing is in Malaysia, and the company has capacity to add without expenses rising linearly with revenue.
